thread:
maya: quick q — i'm proposing a lightweight 'gate-adapters' step in the model onboarding pipeline. idea: run tiny compatibility + fidelity checks (kv-cache layout, tokenizer mapping, basic quantized inference) before we spend GPU hours on full bench. thoughts?

sam: what's the primary win — cost, speed, or catching regressions earlier?

maya: all three. we currently kick off full bench on any new variant. a lot of variants fail for simple reasons (wrong tokenizer, missing kv layout) and waste cycles. gate-adapters would fail fast and attach clear failure tags.

noah: i'm +1 but worry about false negatives. tiny checks might pass while larger seq-lengths hit problems. how do we avoid giving false confidence?

sophie: we can define 2 tiers: smoke (20 prompts, short seq) + extended smoke (longer seq, a few edge-cases). gate-adapters = smoke only. if smoke marginal, auto-trigger extended smoke before full bench.

maya: exactly. propose flow: export -> gate-adapters(smoke) -> on pass schedule full bench; on marginal run extended smoke & notify human; on fail reject with adapter-failure metadata.

maya: sample CLI for the gate-runner:
```
rwd-cli admit --model /tmp/checkpoint.pt \
  --adapters kv,tokenizer,quant \
  --smoke-suite smoke_v1.json \
  --thresholds '{"mem_over":0.05,"ppl_diff":1.2}'
```

ryan: infra question — where should these run? CI small gpu runners or a dedicated low-cost admission pool? running in CI might block merges.

sam: prefer dedicated tiny-gpu pool (admit-gpu-small). keep CI for unit-level checks only.

deploy-bot: note: admitted-pipeline staging job "admit-smoke" created (job id: admit-2026-349).

noah: metadata is key. gate failures must upload artifacts: stdout, short traces, tokenization diffs, and a small reproducible input. we should store those in model-registry under model_id/admit/{ts}.

sophie: tokenizer compatibility is often the culprit. recommendation: canonicalize tokenizer mapping in registry. each model artifact must include tokenizer_id and a md5 of tokenizer config. gate-adapters should run tokenizer roundtrip test: text -> tokens -> decode -> compare normalized text.

maya: agreed. propose minimal artifact schema (string fields): tokenizer_id, dtype, kv_layout, ops_build_id, export_format. registry will validate fields present.

ryan: about thresholds — they should be size-aware. e.g., for <2B models, p99 latency thresholds tighter than >70B. suggest a simple rule engine in gate-runner that picks thresholds by model_size tag.

sam: what's the signal to auto-retry vs escalate? also need an escape hatch for model teams that intentionally ship with slightly different tokenizers.

maya: plan: outcomes = pass / marginal / fail. marginal triggers 3-run expanded-smoke, if still marginal then create a ticket to #eng-ml with @owner and mark as 'needs review'. teams can file a manual override that includes a short justification + tests. overrides are recorded in registry.

noah: can we parallelize multiple adapters per model to keep latency low? run tokenizer + kv checks concurrently, quant check separately since it needs a quantized copy.

sophie: yep, adapters are independent tasks — runner should be async and return aggregated status. also include per-adapter logs and 'blame' tag.

maya: next steps i propose: 1) prototype adapter-runner (sam + noah volunteer), 2) implement smoke_v1 suite and registry schema (sophie + ryan), 3) run 3 recent models through staging for 2 weeks, collect metrics. anyone else volunteer?

sam: i'll take prototype runner. :rocket:

noah: i'll help with runner + artifact uploader. :eyes:

sophie: i'll draft smoke_v1 and registry schema this week.

maya: thanks — i'll file a short RFC with flow diagram and the candidate smoke set and link here when ready.

ryan: one more: add a 'cost-saved' metric to the pipeline so we can quantify GPU-hours avoided. small instrumentation will help justify productionizing.

maya: good call. adding that to the RFC.

deploy-bot: reminder: please include 'admit-smoke' job in staging test matrix before merging.
